question.text: When must you signal, how far ahead, and why must you cancel promptly?

answer.text: Drivers signal every lane change, turn, curb pull-out, slowdown or stop, highway entry or exit, and roadside pull-over, using lamps or bold hand-and-arm gestures from the window, keeping lamps working for darkness, pumping brakes to flag stops, signaling a full one hundred feet ahead, and canceling promptly since stray signals still read as turns.

teaching.text: Signal every lane change, turn, curb pull-out, slowdown, highway entry or exit, and pull-over, a full one hundred feet ahead, then cancel. Remember: signal early, cancel after.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Drivers signal every lane change, turn, curb pull-out, slowdown or stop, highway entry or exit, and roadside pull-over, using lamps or bold hand-and-arm gestures from the window, keeping lamps working for darkness, pumping brakes to flag stops, signaling a full one hundred feet ahead, and canceling promptly since stray signals still read as turns.

question.text: Which situations need signals, and when does the 100-foot signaling rule apply?

answer.text: Use a signal for lane changes, turns, departures from parallel parking, slowing or stopping, highway entry or exit, and pulling to the roadside. Before turning or stopping, keep the signal on for at least one hundred feet; switch off the turn signal after finishing the turn.

teaching.text: Signal for the six listed situations. The continuous 100-foot rule applies before turning or stopping, and the turn signal is canceled after the turn. Remember: 100 feet before turning or stopping.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Use a signal for lane changes, turns, departures from parallel parking, slowing or stopping, highway entry or exit, and pulling to the roadside. Before turning or stopping, keep the signal on for at least one hundred feet; switch off the turn signal after finishing the turn.

question.text: Where is driving on the left side of the road forbidden, and when may you use it?

answer.text: The left side stays forbidden under no-passing markings or signs, with two or more lanes each way, within one hundred feet of intersections, rail crossings, bridges, viaducts, and tunnels, and on hills, curves, and blind spots, while drivers otherwise hug the right except to pass on two- or three-lane streets, on one-way roads, or past blocked right sides.

teaching.text: Keep right except to pass, and never use the left side near intersections, crossings, bridges, viaducts, tunnels, or on hills and curves. Remember: keep right, pass left.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The left side stays forbidden under no-passing markings or signs, with two or more lanes each way, within one hundred feet of intersections, rail crossings, bridges, viaducts, and tunnels, and on hills, curves, and blind spots, while drivers otherwise hug the right except to pass on two- or three-lane streets, on one-way roads, or past blocked right sides.

question.text: Where does the left side close, and when does it open?

answer.text: Stay off the road's left side wherever signs or paint forbid it, where traffic has at least two lanes each way, within one hundred feet of or across a junction or rail crossing, on restricted-view hills or bends, and within one hundred feet of a bridge, viaduct or tunnel. The stated keep-right exceptions are overtaking on a two- or three-lane street, one-way travel, or a blocked right side.

teaching.text: Stay off the road's left side wherever signs or paint forbid it, where traffic has at least two lanes each way, within 100 feet of or across a junction or rail crossing, on restricted-view hills or bends, and within 100 feet of a bridge, viaduct or tunnel. The stated keep-right exceptions are overtaking on a two- or three-lane street, one-way travel, or a blocked right side. Remember: closed near crossings, curves.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Stay off the road's left side wherever signs or paint forbid it, where traffic has at least two lanes each way, within one hundred feet of or across a junction or rail crossing, on restricted-view hills or bends, and within one hundred feet of a bridge, viaduct or tunnel. The stated keep-right exceptions are overtaking on a two- or three-lane street, one-way travel, or a blocked right side.

question.text: What makes a pass safe, and why does a botched pass matter so much?

answer.text: Safe passing waits for clear road, signals lane changes, taps horns against surprises, and returns gently, since botched passes turn head-on and deadly.

teaching.text: Wait for a clear road, signal, tap the horn, and return gently, because a botched pass can turn head-on. Remember: clear road, gentle return.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Safe passing waits for clear road, signals lane changes, taps horns against surprises, and returns gently, since botched passes turn head-on and deadly.

question.text: Which habits make a pass safer?

answer.text: Overtake only with a clear path, signal before moving between lanes, sound a brief horn warning when needed to avoid surprising the driver ahead, and avoid returning too close in front. Bad passing can cause fatal head-on collisions.

teaching.text: Use a clear path, signal before changing lanes, use a horn warning when necessary, and avoid cutting back in too soon. Remember: Horn only when necessary.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Overtake only with a clear path, signal before moving between lanes, sound a brief horn warning when needed to avoid surprising the driver ahead, and avoid returning too close in front. Bad passing can cause fatal head-on collisions.

question.text: What are the steps for passing on a two-lane road?

answer.text: Two-lane passes open with following distance, mirror and blind-spot checks, and a left signal, continue past no-passing checks with enough room to regain the right before oncoming traffic closes inside two hundred feet plus a warning horn tap, and close by passing left, waiting for the overtaken car in the mirror, then signaling right and canceling.

teaching.text: Start from a safe distance, check mirrors and blind spot, signal left, and return only when the passed car shows in your mirror. Remember: check, signal, pass, return.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Two-lane passes open with following distance, mirror and blind-spot checks, and a left signal, continue past no-passing checks with enough room to regain the right before oncoming traffic closes inside two hundred feet plus a warning horn tap, and close by passing left, waiting for the overtaken car in the mirror, then signaling right and canceling.

question.text: How far away must oncoming traffic be before you pass, and what must you see before returning?

answer.text: Overtakers need oncoming traffic beyond two hundred feet before starting, and the passed car visible in the mirror before returning.

teaching.text: Before starting, oncoming traffic must stay beyond two hundred feet; before returning, the passed car must be in your mirror. Remember: two hundred feet, mirror view.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Overtakers need oncoming traffic beyond two hundred feet before starting, and the passed car visible in the mirror before returning.

question.text: When is it lawful to pass on the right?

answer.text: Right-side passing is lawful only when safe on clear wide multi-lane roads, on one-way roads, or along paved shoulders past slowing, stopped, disabled, or left-turning vehicles, and never by leaving the pavement.

teaching.text: Pass on the right only when safe on wide multi-lane roads, one-way roads, or paved shoulders past slow, stopped, or left-turning vehicles. Remember: right passes, never off pavement.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Right-side passing is lawful only when safe on clear wide multi-lane roads, on one-way roads, or along paved shoulders past slowing, stopped, disabled, or left-turning vehicles, and never by leaving the pavement.

question.text: Where may you pass on the right, and what is never allowed?

answer.text: Passing on the right requires safe conditions: a road clear of parked vehicles and other obstructions with room for at least two lanes each way, or a one-way road. A paved shoulder may be used to pass a vehicle slowing or stopped in the highway's traveled area, disabled, or about to turn left. Stay on the pavement.

teaching.text: Passing on the right requires safe conditions: a road clear of parked vehicles and other obstructions with room for at least two lanes each way, or a one-way road. A paved shoulder may be used to pass a vehicle slowing or stopped in the highway's traveled area, disabled, or about to turn left. Stay on the pavement. Remember: stay on the pavement.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Passing on the right requires safe conditions: a road clear of parked vehicles and other obstructions with room for at least two lanes each way, or a one-way road. A paved shoulder may be used to pass a vehicle slowing or stopped in the highway's traveled area, disabled, or about to turn left. Stay on the pavement.

question.text: What must a driver being passed do, and what must the passer avoid?

answer.text: Passed drivers hold speed and lane, ease right on unmarked lanes, and smooth the passer's path, while passers never linger in blind spots but either complete the pass or fall back out of sight.

teaching.text: When passed, hold your speed and lane and ease right on unmarked roads; when passing, never linger in a blind spot. Remember: hold steady, no lingering.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Passed drivers hold speed and lane, ease right on unmarked lanes, and smooth the passer's path, while passers never linger in blind spots but either complete the pass or fall back out of sight.

question.text: How does the passed driver help, and how does the passer clear a blind spot?

answer.text: A driver being overtaken must not speed up and must remain in the same lane. If overtaken on the left where lanes are unmarked, shift safely as far right as possible. When overtaking, clear the other driver's blind spot by completing the pass or dropping back.

teaching.text: A driver being overtaken must not speed up and must remain in the same lane. If overtaken on the left where lanes are unmarked, shift safely as far right as possible. When overtaking, clear the other driver's blind spot by completing the pass or dropping back. Remember: finish or fall back.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A driver being overtaken must not speed up and must remain in the same lane. If overtaken on the left where lanes are unmarked, shift safely as far right as possible. When overtaking, clear the other driver's blind spot by completing the pass or dropping back.

question.text: How should you prepare for a turn, and what if you miss it?

answer.text: Turns start with early decisions against last-second swerves, all-around looks before lane moves, and quick proper-lane entries, skipping any turn missed within half a block.

teaching.text: Decide early, look all around before moving, enter the proper lane quickly, and skip any turn you miss within half a block. Remember: decide early, skip missed turns.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Turns start with early decisions against last-second swerves, all-around looks before lane moves, and quick proper-lane entries, skipping any turn missed within half a block.

question.text: How should you signal, slow, and steer during a turn?

answer.text: Turns continue with signals one hundred feet out, hand signals dropped near the corner for two-handed steering, reasonable pre-turn speed without mid-turn braking or clutching, lane discipline through the maneuver, and proper-lane finishes.

teaching.text: Signal one hundred feet ahead, drop hand signals near the corner, slow before the turn, and keep both hands steering. Remember: both hands through turns.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Turns continue with signals one hundred feet out, hand signals dropped near the corner for two-handed steering, reasonable pre-turn speed without mid-turn braking or clutching, lane discipline through the maneuver, and proper-lane finishes.

question.text: What does committing early to a turn look like, and what do you do when you miss one?

answer.text: Check behind and on both sides before changing lanes for a turn. Choose the proper lane early; if you cannot reach it at least half a block before the turn, continue straight. Give the turn signal at least one hundred feet ahead. A hand signal should show your intent before the junction, then end for the turn so both hands can steer.

teaching.text: Commit early to the proper lane, or skip a missed turn instead of swerving at the last second. Remember: commit early or skip.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Check behind and on both sides before changing lanes for a turn. Choose the proper lane early; if you cannot reach it at least half a block before the turn, continue straight. Give the turn signal at least one hundred feet ahead. A hand signal should show your intent before the junction, then end for the turn so both hands can steer.

question.text: What are the steps for a right turn?

answer.text: Right turns stage early lane signals into the far-right lane, add right signals with slowing one hundred feet out, check both ways, hug the right edge, and steer two-handed.

teaching.text: Move early into the far-right lane, signal and slow one hundred feet out, check both ways, and stay close to the right edge. Remember: hug the right edge.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Right turns stage early lane signals into the far-right lane, add right signals with slowing one hundred feet out, check both ways, hug the right edge, and steer two-handed.

question.text: What are the steps for a left turn on two-way streets?

answer.text: Left turns stage early signals into the center lane, add left signals with slowing one hundred feet out, scan every direction, stay right of center entering while yielding to oncoming traffic, exit right of center into the least-blocking lane, and change lanes afterward as needed.

teaching.text: Move toward the center lane, signal and slow one hundred feet out, yield to oncoming traffic, and stay right of center. Remember: yield, stay right of center.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Left turns stage early signals into the center lane, add left signals with slowing one hundred feet out, scan every direction, stay right of center entering while yielding to oncoming traffic, exit right of center into the least-blocking lane, and change lanes afterward as needed.

question.text: How does the path of a right turn differ from a left turn?

answer.text: Right turns hug the right edge throughout, while left turns yield oncoming traffic and exit right of center into open lanes.

teaching.text: A right turn hugs the right edge; a left turn yields first and exits right of center into the least-blocking lane. Remember: right hugs edge, left yields.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Right turns hug the right edge throughout, while left turns yield oncoming traffic and exit right of center into open lanes.

question.text: Which lanes do you use for a left turn from a one-way street onto a two-way street?

answer.text: Lefts from one-way streets onto two-way streets run from the left lane into the same-direction right lane.

teaching.text: From a one-way street onto a two-way street, start in the left lane and end in the right lane moving your way. Remember: left lane to right lane.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Lefts from one-way streets onto two-way streets run from the left lane into the same-direction right lane.

question.text: Which lane do you enter when turning left onto a one-way street?

answer.text: Lefts onto one-way streets enter the least-blocking lane, and drivers heed markings and signs authorizing multi-lane turns or special lane moves.

teaching.text: Onto a one-way street, enter the lane that blocks traffic least, and follow any markings that allow multi-lane turns. Remember: least-blocking lane.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Lefts onto one-way streets enter the least-blocking lane, and drivers heed markings and signs authorizing multi-lane turns or special lane moves.
